title: Glaucoma Surgical Hierarchy: MIGS, Trabeculectomy & Beyond
summary: A comprehensive clinical breakdown comparing the evolution, efficacy, and safety profiles of modern glaucoma filtration surgeries. Navigating the spectrum from the ultra-minimally invasive to the gold-standard 'filtering' procedures.

sections.title: Red Flags: When MIGS is Contraindicated
content: Advanced or end-stage visual field loss
High target IOP (needs < 10-12 mmHg)
Secondary glaucoma (neovascular/uveitic)
Closed-angle glaucoma (without synechiolysis)
Severe conjunctival scarring (precludes filtering)

sections.title: The Trabeculectomy Gold Standard
content: Step 1: Conjunctival peritomy (Fornix/Limbal base)
Step 2: Scleral flap creation (Partial thickness)
Step 3: MMC/5-FU application for antifibrosis
Step 4: Block excision (Trabeculectomy)
Step 5: Peripheral iridectomy (PI) to prevent iris incarceration
Step 6: Watertight closure of flap and conjunctiva

sections.title: Non-Penetrating Surgery (Deep Sclerectomy)
content: Preserves the integrity of the anterior chamber.
Avoids direct opening of the eyeball (no PI needed).
Decreased risk of shallow AC, hypotony, and endophthalmitis.
Requires highly skilled dissection of the juxtacanalicular tissue.
Often augmented with a collagen implant to maintain space.

sections.title: Clinical Pearls & Recent Evidence
content: Landmark Study: The 'LiGHT' Trial (Lancet 2019) suggests SLT as first-line, but in surgery, trabeculectomy remains superior to MIGS for absolute IOP lowering in advanced cases.
MIGS is best reserved for mild-to-moderate glaucoma in phakic patients who wish to reduce medication burden.
Bleb-related complications (leaks, blebitis) are unique to subconjunctival procedures (Trab/XEN).
GATT (Gonioscopy-Assisted Transluminal Trabeculotomy) is effectively a '360-degree' MIGS with potential for higher efficacy than stent-based procedures.

content.explanation: W - Watch for IOP spikes post-op; A - Antifibrotics (MMC) are critical for filtering success; T - Trabeculectomy is the gold standard for low targets; S - Stents (MIGS) are best for safety profiles.
